fixes.explanation: A second tunic is on the list. Jesus says, “Take no bag for the road, or second tunic, or sandals, or staff…” So no spare tunic goes along. I'd miss my spare apron already.

Praying is a fine thing to do, but it's not the word in this verse. Jesus says they should “…stay at his house until you move on.” It's about staying put at that one house until it's time to go. Stay is the word the blank wants.

Jesus says the opposite. He says, “If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it, but if it is not, let your peace return to you.” So when the home is not worthy, the peace returns to the twelve. It doesn't stay on that home.

Sodom and Gomorrah are the two. Jesus says, “…it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.” This is a serious line, so I'll say it plainly. He is talking about a town that won't welcome the twelve.
Synagogues is the word. Jesus says, “…they will hand you over to their councils and flog you in their synagogues.” He doesn't sugarcoat it. He says it straight.
Courtyards don't show up in this verse. Jesus says, “…they will hand you over to their councils and flog you in their synagogues.” I think this one hurts to hear. The place He names is synagogues.

That's the role Jesus gives. He says, “On My account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.” Witnesses are people who speak about what they know. So being brought before governors and kings puts them there as people who speak about Him.

Ransom isn't mentioned in this verse. Jesus says they will be brought before governors and kings “On My account.” The role He gives them there is witnesses, people who speak about what they know. That's the one.

That's the promise. Jesus says, “…do not worry about how to respond or what to say. In that hour you will be given what to say.” So what to say gets handed to them in that hour. I'd still bring a cookie, but that's just me.
Jesus doesn't mention an angel here. He says, “…it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.” The blank wants Spirit. The speaking happens through the twelve.

That's the promise. Jesus says, “…the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” Persevering means sticking with it all the way. It comes right after He says, “You will be hated by everyone because of My name.”

Jesus says the opposite. He says, “If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household!” He's talking about what the household gets called. If the head of the house got that name, the members aren't left alone. They get even more of it.

Praise isn't what Jesus describes. He says, “If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household!” He's talking about names, and the head of the house has been called Beelzebul. So the household can expect even more of the same, not praise.
